title: A Floating Magnet Feels for Ultraheavy Dark Matter
hook: Most dark matter detectors listen for light particles. POLONAISE levitates a milligram magnet and waits for one shove — reaching masses seven orders of magnitude beyond optical traps.
key_points: POLONAISE levitates a milligram-scale ferromagnet inside a superconducting trap.
Its force sensitivity is 0.07 femtonewtons per root hertz, resolving impulses as small as 1 TeV/c.
Heavy dark matter would announce itself as a single momentum kick, not a steady signal.
The search covers dark matter masses from 10^6 to 10^15 GeV/c-squared with mediators lighter than 30 meV.
Neutron couplings as small as 3.2 x 10^-9 are excluded at 95% confidence.
The mass reach extends seven orders of magnitude beyond optically levitated sensors.
content_html: Dark matter searches are shaped by the mass you assume. Light, wave-like candidates smear across a detector and are found by looking for a faint persistent tone. Ultraheavy candidates — think composite objects far heavier than any known particle — are rarer but individually violent: one would pass through your apparatus and give it a single shove. Detecting that requires a mechanical sensor good enough to notice one tiny kick.
extra_html:
The POLONAISE experiment, reported by Dennis Uitenbroek and colleagues, is that sensor: a milligram-scale ferromagnet levitated in a superconducting trap, with a force sensitivity of 0.07 femtonewtons per root hertz, able to resolve impulses as small as 1 TeV/c. Magnetic levitation of a comparatively heavy mass is the key design choice — it pushes the accessible dark matter mass range seven orders of magnitude past what optically levitated particles can reach.

Their analysis is deliberately conservative: every candidate impulse in the data is counted as a possible dark matter event, and optimum-interval upper limits are drawn from that. For dark matter masses from 10^6 to 10^15 GeV/c-squared interacting through a new mediator lighter than 30 meV, they exclude neutron couplings down to 3.2 x 10^-9 at 95% confidence, which they report as the leading constraints on the dark matter-neutron cross section for composite dark matter. The broader lesson is that tabletop mechanics has become a genuine frontier instrument for particle physics.

related.title: A Dark Matter Detector That Asks Which Way the Hit Came From
related.hook: Neutrons and dark matter can leave identical-looking recoils. MIMAC's answer: reconstruct the direction of each recoil and check whether it points where dark matter should come from.

related.title: A Nanosphere That Feels One Atom Hit It
related.hook: Cool a levitated nanosphere into its quantum ground state and it becomes an exquisite force sensor — sensitive enough to register the kick from a single xenon atom.

related.title: Dark Matter & Dark Energy
related.hook: Everything we can see — stars, planets, people — is only about 5% of the universe. The other 95% is two mysteries we've never directly detected.

related.title: A Quantum Sensor Built to Catch Dark Matter and Ancient Gravitational Waves
related.hook: Two clouds of ultracold atoms, compared against each other, cancel out noise so well that a signal buried in one measurement reappears — aimed at dark matter and ancient gravitational waves.

flashcards.prompt: Why does hunting ultraheavy dark matter call for a milligram magnet rather than a light optically trapped bead?

choices.text: A heavier, magnetically levitated mass can register single momentum impulses across a far wider mass range — seven orders of magnitude beyond optical levitation
Magnets are immune to background vibrations, unlike optical traps
Heavy dark matter only interacts with magnetic materials

flashcards.explanation_html: The paper's headline claim is mass reach: magnetic levitation of a milligram ferromagnet extends the accessible dark matter mass range seven orders of magnitude upward.

flashcards.prompt: What kind of signal does an ultraheavy dark matter particle leave in this detector?
flashcards.back_html: A single momentum impulse — one sharp kick — rather than a continuous wave-like signal. The apparatus resolves impulses as small as 1 TeV/c.

flashcards.prompt: Why treat every candidate impulse as a possible dark matter event?
flashcards.back_html: It is the conservative choice: without subtracting a background model you can still set valid upper limits on the coupling, here as low as 3.2 x 10^-9.
